newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's poison biscuit extortion threat over.
newsitem.headline: Australia's poison biscuit extortion threat over.

text.p: Australian police said on Tuesday they were confident the threat from an extortionist to poison biscuits in supermarkets along the country's east coast was over, but cautioned shoppers to remain vigilant.

"As far as our investigations are concerned, we are confident it (the threat) is over...but the public need to be cautious about the product they purchase," said Queensland police superintendent Ron Pickering.

An extortionist threatened to poison biscuits made by Arnotts, Australia's largest biscuit maker, in the states of New South Wales and Queensland from February 17 unless police involved in a 1991 murder case undertook a lie detector test.
The extortionist said police lied in giving evidence that resulted in Ron Thomas serving two life sentences for a double shooting murder Thomas says he did not commit.
Police said they decided the extortion threat was over on the basis that the extortionist had not contacted them since issuing the threat on February 3.
"Last Thursday, we decided to wait until Monday for any further contact from the extortionist. No contact was made," Pickering told a news conference.
A public appeal by Thomas for the extortionist to stop was also a factor, he said.
However, police said they would continue their investigation into the extortion until they made an arrest.
"We are still treating this extortion as a major investigation," New South Wales police superintendent Jock Milroy told the news conference.
Arnotts withdrew all its products from stores in both states on February 14, three days before the extortionist's deadline, and has dumped millions of packets of biscuits.
The company, 70 percent owned by the Campbell Soup Co of the United States, has said the extortion threat would cost it A$5.0 million (US$3.9 million) a week in sales. (AS1 = US$0.776)
